A retro game library,
made on Linux.

OpenEmux is a free frontend for RetroArch. It keeps your games organized by console, with cover art, and opens them in RetroArch when you pick one, with your controls and shaders already set. It is developed and tested on Linux first; a Windows build is available too, still in beta.

⬇ Download for Linux ⬇ Download for Windows Beta ★ View on GitHub

Free and open source · MIT licensed · AppImage, .deb, .rpm & Flatpak on Linux · installer & portable ZIP on Windows

Features

What OpenEmux does

RetroArch does the emulation. OpenEmux takes care of what is around it: the library, the cores, the controls and the shaders, so there is less to set up by hand.

🎨

Library by console

Games are grouped by console, with cover art downloaded from the libretro thumbnail archive.

✨

Ready on first launch

The first time it opens, OpenEmux creates its configuration and downloads the cores your consoles need, usually in about ten seconds. The rest keep downloading in the background.

🎮

Controls per console

Set keyboard and gamepad buttons for each console in one panel. OpenEmux passes them to RetroArch when a game starts.

📺

Shaders per console

Choose a CRT or scanline shader for each console from a short list, without going through RetroArch's shader menu.

🐧

Made on Linux

Written with GTK4 and Adwaita, following the GNOME guidelines, and tested on Linux before anything else. The Windows build runs the same app and is still in beta.

🔍

BIOS checklist

Shows which BIOS files each console needs and which ones you already have, so a missing file does not end up as a game that silently fails to start.

About the games

Play the games you own

OpenEmux is a front-end for RetroArch, built to make emulation approachable. It is not a source of games — it ships no games, no ROMs, no BIOS files, and never will.

  • Use only content you legally own. Dump your own cartridges and discs, or use backups of games you purchased.
  • Piracy isn't what this is for. Downloading copyrighted games you don't own is illegal in most countries.
  • Emulation helps preserve history. A lot of gaming's art, music and design lives on aging hardware. Keeping it playable is worthwhile, and it works best when it respects the people who made these games.

Settings

ROM folders, BIOS files, controls and shaders are all set in the preferences window, so there are no config files to edit.

Get started

Installing

There are packages for Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora, an AppImage and a Flatpak, and an installer for Windows. On first launch OpenEmux sets up the rest.

Linux

AppImage

Any distro

chmod +x OpenEmux-x86_64.AppImage
./OpenEmux-x86_64.AppImage

No FUSE? Prefix with APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1.

.deb

Debian / Ubuntu

sudo apt install ./openemux_*_amd64.deb

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or newer.

.rpm

Fedora

sudo dnf install ./openemux-*.x86_64.rpm

Fedora 40 or newer.

Flatpak

Sandboxed, auto-updating

flatpak install -y flathub org.libretro.RetroArch
flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists --no-gpg-verify \
  openemux https://guilhermefeitosa66.github.io/openemux-flatpak/repo
flatpak install -y openemux io.github.guilhermefeitosa66.OpenEmux

Updates arrive with flatpak update. A single-file .flatpak bundle is on the Releases page too.

Windows Beta

Both builds carry GTK 4, the Python runtime and RetroArch itself, so there is nothing to install alongside them. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. It is new — if something misbehaves, open an issue.

Installer

The usual way

OpenEmux-*-setup.exe

Installs for your user only, so no administrator prompt. The builds are not code-signed yet: SmartScreen will warn, and More info → Run anyway gets past it.

Portable

Nothing installed

OpenEmux-*-windows-x86_64.zip

Unzip it anywhere and run OpenEmux.exe from the OpenEmux\ folder inside. Good for a USB stick or a machine you cannot install software on.

Checksums

Verify your download

Every release ships a SHA256SUMS file. Put it next to the artifact you downloaded and run:

sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing

OK means the file is exactly what was published. Anything else means it is corrupt or tampered with — don't run it.

On Windows, PowerShell prints the hash and you compare it by eye with the matching line in SHA256SUMS:

Get-FileHash .\OpenEmux-*-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256

Download from Releases →

Prefer building it yourself? make bootstrap && make run — see the build instructions.

Credits

Thanks to RetroArch, libretro & OpenEmu

OpenEmux is inspired by OpenEmu, the emulator frontend for macOS. OpenEmu only runs on macOS, so OpenEmux tries to offer something similar on Linux, and now on Windows too. The emulation itself comes from the RetroArch and libretro projects, and none of this would exist without their work. ❤️

Support the project

OpenEmux is free software

It is free to use, and the code is open under the MIT license. If it is useful to you and you would like to help, a donation pays for some of the time that goes into fixes and new features. Bug reports, translations, code and ideas help just as much. On r/OpenEmux you can ask for help, share your setup or follow what is being worked on.
